test_title: SSC MTS (2022) Official Paper (Held On: 09 May 2023 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution:
The correct answer is 'Option 1' i.e**. 'Many'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The blank must be filled with a word suitable to refer to an uncertain but considerable number of people.
 
• **"Many people"** is the best choice, as it implies a large group of people but doesn't specify a precise number.
 
• This usage also indicates that the sentiment attached - that you can learn about foreign cultures by living abroad - is not universal, but rather held by a significant but indefinite number of people.

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is:* **'Many **people think that we can learn a lot about the culture of a foreign country (2) ________ by living in that country. However, this is not necessarily true. Often, the longer we stay in a (3) ________ country, the more we realize how little we actually know about the culture of that country. Books and talks about other people's (4) ________ can even be dangerous because they concentrate on cultural differences and (5) ________ national character, and sometimes a lot of information they contain is untrue.'*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **"Few" **(Option 2): This wouldn't be the best choice as it indicates a small number of people. The context of the passage suggests a substantial but undefined number of people, better indicated by "many".
 
• **"Every" **(Option 3): This word suggests unanimity (all people). The context of the passage, specifies that this is not a universal belief, ruling out the use of "every".
 
• **"Each" **(Option 4): "Each" refers to all members of a group, considered individually. This doesn't fit here as the passage suggests a multitude, not each individual.
